# xpile_meta_hir - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/^0.1.12/

## Expand description

Canonical meta-HIR.

Every frontend in xpile lowers its language-specific AST to this
shared, intentionally minimal IR. The federated approach (see
`docs/specifications/xpile-architecture-v1.md`) means we start
lossy and grow as hybrid-transpile cases demand.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html)
- [FfiBoundary](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiBoundary.html)
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html)
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.Module.html)
- [Param](https://docs.rs/struct.Param.html)
- [SortKey](https://docs.rs/struct.SortKey.html)
- PMAT-502z (Tranche 2): a `sorted(xs, key=lambda p: e)`sort key — the lambda’s single parameter name plus its (already-lowered) body. The body is lowered with`param`left unbound (an`Ident`), so it works for bodies that don’t need the param’s precise static type (arithmetic,`len(p)`, most builtins); the backend emits`let <param> = __k.clone();`to bind it by value at runtime. Str-method keys (`p.upper()`) are deferred.
- [TryHandler](https://docs.rs/struct.TryHandler.html)
- PMAT-1059: one `except`clause of a multi-handler statement-form`Stmt::TryCatch``as <name>`message binding, and handler statement block.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [BinOp](https://docs.rs/enum.BinOp.html)
- [Dict](https://docs.rs/enum.DictViewKind.html)- View - Kind
- PMAT-502v (Tranche 2): dict view methods carried by `Expr::DictView`
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)
- [FloatOp](https://docs.rs/enum.FloatOp.html)
- PMAT-477 (R8): float arithmetic operators. Carried by
`Expr::FloatBinOp``Add`/`Sub`/`Mul`/`Div`emit plain infix (`f64`saturates, no`checked_*`);`Div`is IEEE-754 true division. PMAT-502br:`FloorDiv`/`Mod`emit Python-correct*floor*semantics (`(a / b).floor()`and`a - b * (a / b).floor()`), which differ from Rust’s truncating`/`int-div and sign-of-dividend`%`— so they are NOT plain infix.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/enum.Item.html)
- [List](https://docs.rs/enum.ListMutateOp.html)- Mutate - Op
- PMAT-502ap (Tranche 2): no-argument in-place list mutators carried by
`Stmt::ListMutate``Vec`method; all return`None`in Python (so they only appear as expression statements).
- [List](https://docs.rs/enum.ListQueryOp.html)- Query - Op
- PMAT-502u (Tranche 2): list query methods carried by `Expr::ListQuery``Int`;`Index`panics on a missing element (Python`ValueError`).
- [Loop](https://docs.rs/enum.LoopKind.html)- Kind
- POSIX shell loop dialects. PMAT-048 / XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001
Layer B. Each variant carries the loop’s control predicate /
item list; the body lives in `Stmt::ShellLoop::body`.
- [NumBuiltin](https://docs.rs/enum.NumBuiltinOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-498 (Tranche 2): scalar numeric builtins carried by
`Expr::NumBuiltin``Abs`takes 1 arg;`Min`/`Max`are variadic (`>= 2`args, PMAT-502cz) and chain`.min`/`.max`over the tail.
- [Pair](https://docs.rs/enum.PairIterKind.html)- Iter - Kind
- PMAT-495 (sprint): the iterator adapter for a `Stmt::ForEachPair`
- [Quoting](https://docs.rs/enum.QuotingStrategy.html)- Strategy
- Per-arg shell quoting choice. Carried by `Expr::QuotedString`so the bashrs-backend renders each arg in the strategy the source indicated. v0.1.0’s bashrs-frontend doesn’t have a real quoting-aware parser yet — it produces`Expr::LitStr`for every arg, and`QuotingStrategy::None`is implicit there. The full strategy set is wired so the v0.2.0 source fold’s real bashrs parser can plug in without IR churn.
- [Radix](https://docs.rs/enum.Radix.html)
- PMAT-502cv: the radix for `hex`/`oct`/`bin`(`Expr::IntRadixStr`).
- [SetOp](https://docs.rs/enum.SetOp.html)
- PMAT-502g (Tranche 2): set-algebra operators carried by `Expr::SetOp``HashSet`method that returns an iterator of borrows, materialized via`.cloned().collect()`into a new owned`HashSet`.
- [SetPred](https://docs.rs/enum.SetPredOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-502ep (Tranche 2): set predicates carried by `Expr::SetPred``bool`. Each maps to a`HashSet`query method; the proper variants additionally require the sets to differ.
- [Source](https://docs.rs/enum.SourceLang.html)- Lang
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/enum.Stmt.html)
- [StrMethod](https://docs.rs/enum.StrMethodOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-492 (sprint): no-argument Python string transform methods,
carried by `Expr::StrMethod`
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.Type.html)
- MVP type lattice. Will grow as frontends demand it. Keep semantically
minimal; map source-language type idiosyncrasies (Python int bigint
promotion, C signed/unsigned, etc.) at the frontend boundary.
PMAT-455 — `Type`is no longer`Copy`because`Type::List(Box<Type>)`is heap-allocated. Callers that previously relied on`*ty`to dereference / copy now use`.clone()`(cheap — most Type values are leaf variants or 1-deep boxes).
- [UnOp](https://docs.rs/enum.UnOp.html)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [collect_](https://docs.rs/fn.collect_block_idents.html)- block_ - idents
- PMAT-736 (HUNT-V11 V11-6): collect every identifier-position name reachable
from `block`into`acc`— both value references (`Expr::Ident`, a`Call`callee) and receiver names (`xs.append(...)`’s`xs`,`d[k] = v`’s`d`, …), plus binding names (a`let`, a loop var). It is the read-only mirror of the`escape_*`walker above: every`escape_name(x)`there becomes`acc.insert(x)`here, so the two stay structurally identical (both are compiler-checked exhaustive over`Stmt`/`Expr`). Used by the frontend’s nested-function lowering to decide whether a nested`def`is self-recursive and whether it captures an enclosing local — over-collection (a binding name, a lambda param) is harmless there, since the caller only intersects the result with the enclosing scope.
- [escape_](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_rust_reserved_idents.html)- rust_ - reserved_ - idents
- PMAT-573: rewrite every identifier in `module`that collides with a Rust keyword to its raw form`r#kw`, so Python locals/params/functions named`type`/`match`/`loop`/… emit valid Rust (and Ruchy). The Rust-family backends call this on a*cloned*module before emission. Struct/enum type names, struct field names, and method names are left unescaped (a keyword-named class/field/method is a separate, rarer fidelity gap).
- [retype_](https://docs.rs/fn.retype_ffi_float_call_sites.html)- ffi_ - float_ - call_ - sites
- Re-type the call sites of `float_ffi`FFI symbols in`module`to F64 so the float-repr path (print`.0`,`let: f64`, float return) is selected. See the PMAT-931 block above. No-op when`float_ffi`is empty.

# xpile_ptx_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-ptx-codegen/0.1.615/target-redirect/xpile_ptx_codegen/

## Expand description

PTX backend.

Lowers Rust meta-HIR (the element-wise scalar kernel shape) to NVIDIA PTX
text targeting `sm_80`+. Layer 5 compile contract:
`contracts/compile-rust-to-ptx-mma-v1.yaml`.

**Real emitter (PMAT-961):** [`XpilePtxEmitter`] is a genuine
meta-HIR → PTX text lowering ([ emit::emit_kernel](https://docs.rs/fn.emit_kernel.html)) — the NVIDIA sibling of

`xpile-wasm-codegen`’s hand-emitted WAT. It emits a complete
`ptxas`-assemblable `.visible .entry xpile_kernel` module (`.version` /
`.target sm_<cc>` derived from [/](https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_backend/enum.HwProfile.html#variant.Ptx)

`HwProfile::Ptx``.address_size 64`,
`ld.global` → scalar arithmetic → `st.global`) for the scalar element-wise
subset, and REFUSES aggregates / control flow Lean-style. It replaces the
v0.1.0 `ScaffoldPtxEmitter` comment placeholder (retired).**Architecture (PMAT-264 / Section 29):** [ PtxBackend](https://docs.rs/struct.PtxBackend.html) wraps a

[so emission routes through the same general/specialist quorum framework. The real [](https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_backend/struct.MultiEmitterBackend.html)

`MultiEmitterBackend``XpilePtxEmitter`] is the
`general` slot; `aprender-gpu` would slot into the `specialist` position;
no changes to [’s public API.](https://docs.rs/struct.PtxBackend.html)

`PtxBackend`**§29 anti-correlation witness (PMAT-961):** [ PtxBackend::new_ptx_diffexec_witness](https://docs.rs/struct.PtxBackend.html#method.new_ptx_diffexec_witness)
installs the

[, which diffs xpile’s OWN hand-emitted PTX (run via the CUDA Driver API) against the nvcc-compiled CUDA-C](https://docs.rs/struct.PtxDiffExecEngine.html)

`PtxDiffExecEngine``xpile_kernel`
— two **categorically-independent codegen toolchains**for the same kernel, upgrading PMAT-949’s two-CUDA-C-kernels-same-nvcc check to a genuinely independent pair. cuda-oxide (PMAT-480) becomes the 3rd independent emitter on top of this pair (its own nightly slice).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Nvcc](https://docs.rs/struct.NvccCudaDiffExecEngine.html)- Cuda - Diff - Exec - Engine
- A real CUDA `DiffExecEngine`: nvcc-compiles each emitter’s CUDA-C kernel, runs both on the GPU, and numerically compares the outputs. This is the executed Run≥1 witness for`C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA`.
- [PtxBackend](https://docs.rs/struct.PtxBackend.html)
- PTX backend — `Backend`impl wrapping a`MultiEmitterBackend``rustc_codegen_nvvm`+`aprender-gpu`quorum will use.
- [PtxDiff](https://docs.rs/struct.PtxDiffExecEngine.html)- Exec - Engine
- A real anti-correlation CUDA `DiffExecEngine`: runs xpile’s hand-emitted PTX (via the CUDA Driver API) AND the nvcc-compiled CUDA-C kernel, then diffs the executed outputs. This is the categorical-independence upgrade of the §29 PTX lane (PMAT-961).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [PtxValidation](https://docs.rs/enum.PtxValidationError.html)- Error
- Reasons emitted PTX text fails the `validate_ptx`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [FIXTURE_](https://docs.rs/constant.FIXTURE_INPUT.html)- INPUT
- The deterministic fixture input vector both kernels run over. Fixed so the witness is reproducible; the values exercise negatives, zero, a fraction, and a larger magnitude.
- [KERNEL_](https://docs.rs/constant.KERNEL_NAME.html)- NAME
- The kernel entry-point name. Bit-identical to the nvcc CUDA-C
`xpile_kernel`(the PMAT-949 path) so the anti-correlation quorum loads the same symbol from both toolchains.
- [NVPTX_](https://docs.rs/constant.NVPTX_TARGET.html)- TARGET
- The rustc target triple for NVIDIA PTX (LLVM NVPTX back-end).
- [PTX_](https://docs.rs/constant.PTX_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- PTX ISA version FLOOR. 8.0 is supported by CUDA 11.8+ and assembles for
every `.target`in the contract’s sm_80..sm_90 range (sm_89/sm_90 require ISA ≥ 7.8; 8.0 is the safe common floor with headroom). Pure text — the real`ptxas`on the box validates it (see`crate::PtxDiffExecEngine`
- [RUSTC_](https://docs.rs/constant.RUSTC_NVPTX_KERNEL_SRC.html)- NVPTX_ - KERNEL_ - SRC
- The Rust kernel source compiled to PTX by nightly `rustc`’s NVPTX back-end.
- [SAXPY_](https://docs.rs/constant.SAXPY_CUDA_C_KERNEL.html)- CUDA_ - C_ - KERNEL
- The nvcc-compilable CUDA-C `xpile_kernel`for the canonical`out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1`saxpy kernel (the specialist half of the §29 PTX anti-correlation pair).`pub`so the PMAT-963 cross-hardware witness pairs it with xpile’s hand-emitted PTX and runs both on the gx10 (GB10 / sm_121) fleet host — the same categorically-independent pair as the local sm_89 arm, on a different architecture.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [cuda_](https://docs.rs/fn.cuda_toolchain_available.html)- toolchain_ - available
- `true`when both- `nvcc`and- `nvidia-smi`are invocable — the gate that decides whether- `NvccCudaDiffExecEngine`- `have_python_and_rustc`/ cc-availability graceful-skip pattern: absence is a clean skip (CI), presence runs the witness (local GPU box).
- [emit_](https://docs.rs/fn.emit_kernel.html)- kernel
- Lower a meta-HIR `Function``compute_capability`(e.g.`sm_89`).
- [emit_](https://docs.rs/fn.emit_rustc_nvptx_ptx.html)- rustc_ - nvptx_ - ptx
- The rustc-nvptx PTX (from the cached [`probe`]).`Err(reason)`if the toolchain / target`rust-std`is missing or the compile failed (the witness turns that into a clean skip).
- [ptx_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptx_looks_real.html)- looks_ - real
- `true`when- `text`looks like real PTX (carries a- `.version`directive) rather than the v0.1.0 scaffold comment placeholder.
- [ptx_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptx_version_for.html)- version_ - for
- PTX ISA version that assembles for `compute_capability`’s`.target`—**derived, never hard-coded**(the same honesty discipline as the`.target`directive itself, PMAT-963).
- [ptxas_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptxas_arch.html)- arch
- The `ptxas -arch=<…>`value for a PTX`.target`compute capability —**derived, never hard-coded**(PMAT-481). The`ptxas`assemble step uses this so the assembled arch always matches the emitted`.target`.
- [ptxas_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptxas_assemble.html)- assemble
- PMAT-961 — assemble `ptx_text`with the real`ptxas`for`compute_capability`, returning`Ok(())`on a clean assemble or`Err(stderr)`on rejection. The caller gates on`ptxas_available``wat2wasm`and the WGSL lane from naga — proof the hand-emitted PTX is well-formed for the NVIDIA assembler, not just our own structural`validate_ptx`
- [ptxas_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptxas_available.html)- available
- `true`when- `ptxas`(the offline PTX assembler) is invocable — the gate for the PMAT-961 offline assemble-validation test. Mirrors the cc/wat2wasm/nvcc graceful-skip helpers: absence is a clean skip (free CI has no CUDA toolkit), presence assembles the emitted PTX for real. This is the PTX analog of- `wat2wasm`-assembles-WAT / naga-validates-WGSL.
- [rustc_](https://docs.rs/fn.rustc_nvptx_available.html)- nvptx_ - available
- `true`when nightly- `rustc`’s- `nvptx64-nvidia-cuda`target can ACTUALLY compile a Rust kernel to PTX on this box (a cached real compile — never just “the target is listed”, which is always true even with the- `rust-std`absent). Absent → the gated witnesses cleanly skip.
- [saxpy_](https://docs.rs/fn.saxpy_kernel_fn.html)- kernel_ - fn
- Build the canonical `out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1`f64 kernel function the witness emitters share (so xpile PTX and nvcc CUDA-C attest the same semantics).`pub`so the PMAT-963 cross-hardware witness emits xpile’s hand-emitted PTX for the gx10 (sm_121) target from the SAME meta-HIR the local sm_89 arm uses.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_ptx.html)- ptx
- PMAT-481 — structural well-formedness check on emitted PTX text:
`.version`,`.target`matching`compute_capability`,`.address_size 64`, and at least one`.visible .entry`. Pure text — no GPU, no`ptxas`. Gate on`ptx_looks_real`

`PtxDiffExecEngine``xpile_kernel`
— two **categorically-independent codegen toolchains**for the same kernel, upgrading PMAT-949’s two-CUDA-C-kernels-same-nvcc check to a genuinely independent pair. cuda-oxide (PMAT-480) becomes the 3rd independent emitter on top of this pair (its own nightly slice).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Nvcc](https://docs.rs/struct.NvccCudaDiffExecEngine.html)- Cuda - Diff - Exec - Engine
- A real CUDA `DiffExecEngine`: nvcc-compiles each emitter’s CUDA-C kernel, runs both on the GPU, and numerically compares the outputs. This is the executed Run≥1 witness for`C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA`.
- [PtxBackend](https://docs.rs/struct.PtxBackend.html)
- PTX backend — `Backend`impl wrapping a`MultiEmitterBackend``rustc_codegen_nvvm`+`aprender-gpu`quorum will use.
- [PtxDiff](https://docs.rs/struct.PtxDiffExecEngine.html)- Exec - Engine
- A real anti-correlation CUDA `DiffExecEngine`: runs xpile’s hand-emitted PTX (via the CUDA Driver API) AND the nvcc-compiled CUDA-C kernel, then diffs the executed outputs. This is the categorical-independence upgrade of the §29 PTX lane (PMAT-961).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [PtxValidation](https://docs.rs/enum.PtxValidationError.html)- Error
- Reasons emitted PTX text fails the `validate_ptx`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [FIXTURE_](https://docs.rs/constant.FIXTURE_INPUT.html)- INPUT
- The deterministic fixture input vector both kernels run over. Fixed so the witness is reproducible; the values exercise negatives, zero, a fraction, and a larger magnitude.
- [KERNEL_](https://docs.rs/constant.KERNEL_NAME.html)- NAME
- The kernel entry-point name. Bit-identical to the nvcc CUDA-C
`xpile_kernel`(the PMAT-949 path) so the anti-correlation quorum loads the same symbol from both toolchains.
- [NVPTX_](https://docs.rs/constant.NVPTX_TARGET.html)- TARGET
- The rustc target triple for NVIDIA PTX (LLVM NVPTX back-end).
- [PTX_](https://docs.rs/constant.PTX_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- PTX ISA version FLOOR. 8.0 is supported by CUDA 11.8+ and assembles for
every `.target`in the contract’s sm_80..sm_90 range (sm_89/sm_90 require ISA ≥ 7.8; 8.0 is the safe common floor with headroom). Pure text — the real`ptxas`on the box validates it (see`crate::PtxDiffExecEngine`
- [RUSTC_](https://docs.rs/constant.RUSTC_NVPTX_KERNEL_SRC.html)- NVPTX_ - KERNEL_ - SRC
- The Rust kernel source compiled to PTX by nightly `rustc`’s NVPTX back-end.
- [SAXPY_](https://docs.rs/constant.SAXPY_CUDA_C_KERNEL.html)- CUDA_ - C_ - KERNEL
- The nvcc-compilable CUDA-C `xpile_kernel`for the canonical`out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1`saxpy kernel (the specialist half of the §29 PTX anti-correlation pair).`pub`so the PMAT-963 cross-hardware witness pairs it with xpile’s hand-emitted PTX and runs both on the gx10 (GB10 / sm_121) fleet host — the same categorically-independent pair as the local sm_89 arm, on a different architecture.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [cuda_](https://docs.rs/fn.cuda_toolchain_available.html)- toolchain_ - available
- `true`when both- `nvcc`and- `nvidia-smi`are invocable — the gate that decides whether- `NvccCudaDiffExecEngine`- `have_python_and_rustc`/ cc-availability graceful-skip pattern: absence is a clean skip (CI), presence runs the witness (local GPU box).
- [emit_](https://docs.rs/fn.emit_kernel.html)- kernel
- Lower a meta-HIR `Function``compute_capability`(e.g.`sm_89`).
- [emit_](https://docs.rs/fn.emit_rustc_nvptx_ptx.html)- rustc_ - nvptx_ - ptx
- The rustc-nvptx PTX (from the cached [`probe`]).`Err(reason)`if the toolchain / target`rust-std`is missing or the compile failed (the witness turns that into a clean skip).
- [ptx_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptx_looks_real.html)- looks_ - real
- `true`when- `text`looks like real PTX (carries a- `.version`directive) rather than the v0.1.0 scaffold comment placeholder.
- [ptx_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptx_version_for.html)- version_ - for
- PTX ISA version that assembles for `compute_capability`’s`.target`—**derived, never hard-coded**(the same honesty discipline as the`.target`directive itself, PMAT-963).
- [ptxas_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptxas_arch.html)- arch
- The `ptxas -arch=<…>`value for a PTX`.target`compute capability —**derived, never hard-coded**(PMAT-481). The`ptxas`assemble step uses this so the assembled arch always matches the emitted`.target`.
- [ptxas_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptxas_assemble.html)- assemble
- PMAT-961 — assemble `ptx_text`with the real`ptxas`for`compute_capability`, returning`Ok(())`on a clean assemble or`Err(stderr)`on rejection. The caller gates on`ptxas_available``wat2wasm`and the WGSL lane from naga — proof the hand-emitted PTX is well-formed for the NVIDIA assembler, not just our own structural`validate_ptx`
- [ptxas_](https://docs.rs/fn.ptxas_available.html)- available
- `true`when- `ptxas`(the offline PTX assembler) is invocable — the gate for the PMAT-961 offline assemble-validation test. Mirrors the cc/wat2wasm/nvcc graceful-skip helpers: absence is a clean skip (free CI has no CUDA toolkit), presence assembles the emitted PTX for real. This is the PTX analog of- `wat2wasm`-assembles-WAT / naga-validates-WGSL.
- [rustc_](https://docs.rs/fn.rustc_nvptx_available.html)- nvptx_ - available
- `true`when nightly- `rustc`’s- `nvptx64-nvidia-cuda`target can ACTUALLY compile a Rust kernel to PTX on this box (a cached real compile — never just “the target is listed”, which is always true even with the- `rust-std`absent). Absent → the gated witnesses cleanly skip.
- [saxpy_](https://docs.rs/fn.saxpy_kernel_fn.html)- kernel_ - fn
- Build the canonical `out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1`f64 kernel function the witness emitters share (so xpile PTX and nvcc CUDA-C attest the same semantics).`pub`so the PMAT-963 cross-hardware witness emits xpile’s hand-emitted PTX for the gx10 (sm_121) target from the SAME meta-HIR the local sm_89 arm uses.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_ptx.html)- ptx
- PMAT-481 — structural well-formedness check on emitted PTX text:
`.version`,`.target`matching`compute_capability`,`.address_size 64`, and at least one`.visible .entry`. Pure text — no GPU, no`ptxas`. Gate on`ptx_looks_real`

# lib.rs - source

# xpile_ptx_codegen/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! PTX backend.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! Lowers Rust meta-HIR (the element-wise scalar kernel shape) to NVIDIA PTX
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! text targeting `sm_80`+. Layer 5 compile contract:
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! `contracts/compile-rust-to-ptx-mma-v1.yaml`.
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//!
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! **Real emitter (PMAT-961):** [`XpilePtxEmitter`] is a genuine
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! meta-HIR → PTX text lowering ([`emit::emit_kernel`]) — the NVIDIA sibling of
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! `xpile-wasm-codegen`'s hand-emitted WAT. It emits a complete
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! `ptxas`-assemblable `.visible .entry xpile_kernel` module (`.version` /
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! `.target sm_<cc>` derived from [`HwProfile::Ptx`] / `.address_size 64`,
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! `ld.global` → scalar arithmetic → `st.global`) for the scalar element-wise
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! subset, and REFUSES aggregates / control flow Lean-style. It replaces the
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! v0.1.0 `ScaffoldPtxEmitter` comment placeholder (retired).
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! **Architecture (PMAT-264 / Section 29):** [`PtxBackend`] wraps a
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! [`MultiEmitterBackend`] so emission routes through the same
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! general/specialist quorum framework. The real [`XpilePtxEmitter`] is the
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! `general` slot; `aprender-gpu` would slot into the `specialist` position;
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! no changes to [`PtxBackend`]'s public API.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! **§29 anti-correlation witness (PMAT-961):** [`PtxBackend::new_ptx_diffexec_witness`]
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! installs the [`PtxDiffExecEngine`], which diffs xpile's OWN hand-emitted PTX
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! (run via the CUDA Driver API) against the nvcc-compiled CUDA-C `xpile_kernel`
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! — two **categorically-independent codegen toolchains** for the same kernel,
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! upgrading PMAT-949's two-CUDA-C-kernels-same-nvcc check to a genuinely
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! independent pair. cuda-oxide (PMAT-480) becomes the 3rd independent emitter
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! on top of this pair (its own nightly slice).
[29](https://docs.rs#29)

[45](https://docs.rs#45)// nvptx64-nvidia-cuda target (LLVM NVPTX back-end). External subprocess, gated.

[50](https://docs.rs#50)/// PTX backend — `Backend` impl wrapping a [`MultiEmitterBackend`] so
[51](https://docs.rs#51)/// the v0.1.0 scaffold drives through the same routing the future
[52](https://docs.rs#52)/// `rustc_codegen_nvvm` + `aprender-gpu` quorum will use.
[53](https://docs.rs#53)pub struct PtxBackend {
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    inner: MultiEmitterBackend,
[55](https://docs.rs#55)}
[56](https://docs.rs#56)
[57](https://docs.rs#57)impl Default for PtxBackend {
[58](https://docs.rs#58)    fn default() -> Self {
[59](https://docs.rs#59)        Self::new()
[60](https://docs.rs#60)    }
[61](https://docs.rs#61)}
[62](https://docs.rs#62)
[63](https://docs.rs#63)impl PtxBackend {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[65](https://docs.rs#65)        Self {
[66](https://docs.rs#66)            inner: MultiEmitterBackend::new_single(Target::Ptx, Box::new(XpilePtxEmitter)),
[67](https://docs.rs#67)        }
[68](https://docs.rs#68)    }
[69](https://docs.rs#69)
[70](https://docs.rs#70)    /// PMAT-280 — End-to-end validation constructor for Section 29's
[71](https://docs.rs#71)    /// multi-emitter routing.
[72](https://docs.rs#72)    ///
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    /// Builds a `PtxBackend` whose `MultiEmitterBackend` carries the real
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    /// [`XpilePtxEmitter`] in the `general` slot AND a
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    /// [`MatmulSpecialistEmitter`] in the `specialist` slot under
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    /// `QuorumPolicy::PreferSpecialist`. The specialist matches only
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    /// modules whose name starts with `matmul_` — the shape filter
[78](https://docs.rs#78)    /// real specialists like `aprender-gpu` would use to claim
[79](https://docs.rs#79)    /// GEMM-shaped kernels.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)    ///
[81](https://docs.rs#81)    /// This isn't registered in `default_session()` — production at
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    /// v0.1.0+ still uses [`PtxBackend::new`]. The constructor exists
[83](https://docs.rs#83)    /// so tests + future integrations can exercise the
[84](https://docs.rs#84)    /// `MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist` path against real
[85](https://docs.rs#85)    /// production code (not just mock tests). It's the smallest
[86](https://docs.rs#86)    /// concrete proof that the §29 routing layer is end-to-end
[87](https://docs.rs#87)    /// usable, ahead of the heavy `rustc_codegen_nvvm` / `aprender-gpu`
[88](https://docs.rs#88)    /// integrations that will eventually replace these placeholders.
[89](https://docs.rs#89)    pub fn new_with_matmul_specialist() -> Self {
[90](https://docs.rs#90)        Self {
[91](https://docs.rs#91)            inner: MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[92](https://docs.rs#92)                Target::Ptx,
[93](https://docs.rs#93)                Box::new(XpilePtxEmitter),
[94](https://docs.rs#94)                Box::new(MatmulSpecialistEmitter),
[95](https://docs.rs#95)                QuorumPolicy::PreferSpecialist,
[96](https://docs.rs#96)            ),
[97](https://docs.rs#97)        }
[98](https://docs.rs#98)    }
[99](https://docs.rs#99)
[100](https://docs.rs#100)    /// PMAT-961 — the TRUE anti-correlation §29 PTX witness constructor.
[101](https://docs.rs#101)    ///
[102](https://docs.rs#102)    /// Builds a `PtxBackend` whose `MultiEmitterBackend` carries TWO
[103](https://docs.rs#103)    /// categorically-independent emitters for the same `out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1`
[104](https://docs.rs#104)    /// kernel — [`XpileSaxpyPtxEmitter`] (general: xpile's OWN hand-emitted
[105](https://docs.rs#105)    /// PTX) and [`CudaSaxpyGeneralEmitter`] (specialist: nvcc-compilable
[106](https://docs.rs#106)    /// CUDA-C) — under `QuorumPolicy::DiffExec`, with a [`PtxDiffExecEngine`]
[107](https://docs.rs#107)    /// installed. The engine runs the xpile PTX via the CUDA Driver API and the
[108](https://docs.rs#108)    /// nvcc CUDA-C via the Runtime API, both on the GPU, and asserts the
[109](https://docs.rs#109)    /// executed outputs agree.
[110](https://docs.rs#110)    ///
[111](https://docs.rs#111)    /// This is the categorical-independence upgrade of
[112](https://docs.rs#112)    /// [`PtxBackend::new_cuda_diffexec_witness`] (PMAT-949): that diffed two
[113](https://docs.rs#113)    /// CUDA-C kernels compiled by the SAME nvcc; this diffs two DIFFERENT
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    /// codegen toolchains (xpile hand-emit vs nvcc). On a non-GPU host the
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    /// engine is NOT installed → the benign `NotRun { no-engine }`, free CI
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    /// stays green.
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    pub fn new_ptx_diffexec_witness() -> Self {
[118](https://docs.rs#118)        let mut inner = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[119](https://docs.rs#119)            Target::Ptx,
[120](https://docs.rs#120)            Box::new(XpileSaxpyPtxEmitter),
[121](https://docs.rs#121)            Box::new(CudaSaxpyGeneralEmitter),
[122](https://docs.rs#122)            QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance: 1.0e-3 },
[123](https://docs.rs#123)        );
[124](https://docs.rs#124)        if cuda_toolchain_available() {
[125](https://docs.rs#125)            inner = inner.with_diff_exec_engine(std::sync::Arc::new(PtxDiffExecEngine::new()));
[126](https://docs.rs#126)        }
[127](https://docs.rs#127)        Self { inner }
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    }
[129](https://docs.rs#129)
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    /// PMAT-1006 — the §29 PTX quorum with the **rustc-nvptx** (LLVM NVPTX
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    /// back-end) arm as a THIRD production voter, so the anti-correlation guard
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    /// runs THREE categorically-independent codegen toolchains (xpile hand-emit
[133](https://docs.rs#133)    /// text / nvcc CUDA-C via NVVM / rustc via modern LLVM NVPTX) in production,
[134](https://docs.rs#134)    /// not just at witness level.
[135](https://docs.rs#135)    ///
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    /// HONEST reporting: rustc-nvptx is a reported voter ONLY when it actually
[137](https://docs.rs#137)    /// runs. On a CUDA box WITH nightly rustc + the `nvptx64-nvidia-cuda` target,
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    /// the DiffExec runs all three and `QuorumStatus::Multi` names 3 emitters;
[139](https://docs.rs#139)    /// WITHOUT rustc-nvptx it falls back to the 2-way quorum (2 emitters);
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    /// WITHOUT a GPU it records `NotRun` (2 emitters, no vote) — never a false
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    /// third voter.
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    pub fn new_ptx_3way_diffexec_witness() -> Self {
[143](https://docs.rs#143)        let mut inner = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[144](https://docs.rs#144)            Target::Ptx,
[145](https://docs.rs#145)            Box::new(XpileSaxpyPtxEmitter),
[146](https://docs.rs#146)            Box::new(CudaSaxpyGeneralEmitter),
[147](https://docs.rs#147)            QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance: 1.0e-3 },
[148](https://docs.rs#148)        );
[149](https://docs.rs#149)        if cuda_toolchain_available() {
[150](https://docs.rs#150)            if rustc_nvptx_available() {
[151](https://docs.rs#151)                inner = inner
[152](https://docs.rs#152)                    .with_diff_exec_engine(std::sync::Arc::new(PtxDiffExecEngine::new_three_way()))
[153](https://docs.rs#153)                    .with_diff_exec_extra_emitters(vec!["rustc-nvptx".to_string()]);
[154](https://docs.rs#154)            } else {
[155](https://docs.rs#155)                inner = inner.with_diff_exec_engine(std::sync::Arc::new(PtxDiffExecEngine::new()));
[156](https://docs.rs#156)            }
[157](https://docs.rs#157)        }
[158](https://docs.rs#158)        Self { inner }
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    }
[160](https://docs.rs#160)
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    /// PMAT-962 — the anti-correlation §29 PTX witness for a NEW construct:
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    /// **control flow** (`if`/`else` + comparison), not just straight-line
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    /// arithmetic.
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    ///
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    /// The same categorical-independence design as
[166](https://docs.rs#166)    /// [`PtxBackend::new_ptx_diffexec_witness`] but over the relu kernel
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    /// `out[i] = (in[i] > 0) ? in[i] : 0`:
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    ///   - general: [`XpileReluPtxEmitter`] — xpile's OWN hand-emitted PTX, with
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    ///     a real `setp.gt.f64` + `@!%p bra` branch + a shared result register
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    ///     (the phi-via-register idiom).
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    ///   - specialist: [`CudaReluGeneralEmitter`] — nvcc-compiled CUDA-C using a
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    ///     C `?:` ternary.
[173](https://docs.rs#173)    ///
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    /// Two codegen toolchains with NO shared frontend that must agree on the
[175](https://docs.rs#175)    /// branchy kernel — exercising the PMAT-962 control-flow lowering end-to-end
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    /// on real silicon. Relu over [`FIXTURE_INPUT`] is exactly representable so
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    /// the executed outputs agree bit-for-bit. Graceful-skip off-GPU (no engine
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    /// installed → benign `NotRun`, free CI green).
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    pub fn new_ptx_if_diffexec_witness() -> Self {
[180](https://docs.rs#180)        let mut inner = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[181](https://docs.rs#181)            Target::Ptx,
[182](https://docs.rs#182)            Box::new(XpileReluPtxEmitter),
[183](https://docs.rs#183)            Box::new(CudaReluGeneralEmitter),
[184](https://docs.rs#184)            QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance: 1.0e-3 },
[185](https://docs.rs#185)        );
[186](https://docs.rs#186)        if cuda_toolchain_available() {
[187](https://docs.rs#187)            inner = inner.with_diff_exec_engine(std::sync::Arc::new(PtxDiffExecEngine::new()));
[188](https://docs.rs#188)        }
[189](https://docs.rs#189)        Self { inner }
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    }
[191](https://docs.rs#191)
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    /// PMAT-949 — the executed GPU-witness constructor (§29).
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    ///
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    /// Builds a `PtxBackend` whose `MultiEmitterBackend` carries two
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// REAL CUDA-C kernel emitters — [`CudaSaxpyGeneralEmitter`]
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    /// (general) and [`CudaSaxpySpecialistEmitter`] (specialist) — under
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    /// `QuorumPolicy::DiffExec`, with a [`NvccCudaDiffExecEngine`]
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    /// installed. Both emitters compute the same semantics
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// (`out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1`) via *categorically different* CUDA-C
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// implementations (one `fmaf`, one explicit `mul`+`add`), so the
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// `DiffExec` quorum runs BOTH on the GPU and asserts they agree —
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// the falsifying multi-emitter check the §29 design specs.
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    ///
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    /// This is the constructor that, when run on a CUDA box, produces a
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    /// real [`xpile_backend::DiffExecResult::Match`] instead of the
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    /// `NotRun { no-engine }` placeholder — closing the audit-design.md
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    /// §4 / §62 "Run=1 / DiffExecResult::NotRun" caveat for
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    /// `C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA`.
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    ///
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// On a host without `nvcc` + `nvidia-smi` the engine is NOT
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// installed (the `MultiEmitterBackend` keeps `diff_exec_engine =
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    /// None`), so the backend records the benign `NotRun { no-engine }`
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    /// and free CI stays green — the cc/python3 graceful-skip posture.
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    pub fn new_cuda_diffexec_witness() -> Self {
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        let mut inner = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[216](https://docs.rs#216)            Target::Ptx,
[217](https://docs.rs#217)            Box::new(CudaSaxpyGeneralEmitter),
[218](https://docs.rs#218)            Box::new(CudaSaxpySpecialistEmitter),
[219](https://docs.rs#219)            QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance: 1.0e-3 },
[220](https://docs.rs#220)        );
[221](https://docs.rs#221)        if cuda_toolchain_available() {
[222](https://docs.rs#222)            inner = inner.with_diff_exec_engine(std::sync::Arc::new(NvccCudaDiffExecEngine::new()));
[223](https://docs.rs#223)        }
[224](https://docs.rs#224)        Self { inner }
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    }
[226](https://docs.rs#226)}
[227](https://docs.rs#227)
[228](https://docs.rs#228)impl Backend for PtxBackend {
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
[230](https://docs.rs#230)        "ptx"
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    }
[232](https://docs.rs#232)
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    fn targets(&self) -> &[Target] {
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        &[Target::Ptx]
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    }
[236](https://docs.rs#236)
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    fn lower(&self, module: &Module, config: &BackendConfig) -> Result<Artifact, BackendError> {
[238](https://docs.rs#238)        // Reject inputs without an HwProfile::Ptx eagerly — the
[239](https://docs.rs#239)        // scaffold emitter can't synthesize a compute_capability and
[240](https://docs.rs#240)        // the contract requires one.
[241](https://docs.rs#241)        match &config.hardware {
[242](https://docs.rs#242)            Some(HwProfile::Ptx { .. }) => {}
[243](https://docs.rs#243)            _ => return Err(BackendError::MissingHardware(Target::Ptx)),
[244](https://docs.rs#244)        }
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        self.inner.lower(module, config)
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    }
[247](https://docs.rs#247)}
[248](https://docs.rs#248)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)/// PMAT-961 — the REAL meta-HIR → PTX emitter (general slot).
[250](https://docs.rs#250)///
[251](https://docs.rs#251)/// Lowers the module's single kernel [`Function`] of the element-wise scalar
[252](https://docs.rs#252)/// shape to a complete `ptxas`-assemblable PTX module via
[253](https://docs.rs#253)/// [`emit::emit_kernel`]. Retires the v0.1.0 `ScaffoldPtxEmitter` comment
[254](https://docs.rs#254)/// placeholder. Refuses (hard `BackendError`) any module that isn't a single
[255](https://docs.rs#255)/// scalar element-wise function — never wrong PTX.
[256](https://docs.rs#256)struct XpilePtxEmitter;
[257](https://docs.rs#257)
[258](https://docs.rs#258)impl TargetEmitter for XpilePtxEmitter {
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    fn name(&self) -> &str {
[260](https://docs.rs#260)        "xpile-ptx-codegen"
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    }
[262](https://docs.rs#262)
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    fn try_emit(
[264](https://docs.rs#264)        &self,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        module: &Module,
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        config: &BackendConfig,
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    ) -> Option<Result<EmittedText, BackendError>> {
[268](https://docs.rs#268)        let compute_capability = match &config.hardware {
[269](https://docs.rs#269)            Some(HwProfile::Ptx { compute_capability }) => compute_capability,
[270](https://docs.rs#270)            _ => return Some(Err(BackendError::MissingHardware(Target::Ptx))),
[271](https://docs.rs#271)        };
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        // The element-wise PTX subset emits exactly one kernel function. An
[273](https://docs.rs#273)        // empty / multi-function / non-function module is refused honestly.
[274](https://docs.rs#274)        let funcs: Vec<&Function> = module
[275](https://docs.rs#275)            .items
[276](https://docs.rs#276)            .iter()
[277](https://docs.rs#277)            .filter_map(|i| match i {
[278](https://docs.rs#278)                Item::Function(f) => Some(f),
[279](https://docs.rs#279)                _ => None,
[280](https://docs.rs#280)            })
[281](https://docs.rs#281)            .collect();
[282](https://docs.rs#282)        let f = match funcs.as_slice() {
[283](https://docs.rs#283)            [single] => *single,
[284](https://docs.rs#284)            [] => {
[285](https://docs.rs#285)                return Some(Err(BackendError::Lower(
[286](https://docs.rs#286)                    "xpile-ptx-codegen: module has no kernel function (the PTX element-wise \
[287](https://docs.rs#287)                     subset emits exactly one scalar element-wise function)"
[288](https://docs.rs#288)                        .to_string(),
[289](https://docs.rs#289)                )))
[290](https://docs.rs#290)            }
[291](https://docs.rs#291)            _ => {
[292](https://docs.rs#292)                return Some(Err(BackendError::Lower(
[293](https://docs.rs#293)                    "xpile-ptx-codegen: module has multiple functions (the PTX element-wise \
[294](https://docs.rs#294)                     subset emits exactly one kernel)"
[295](https://docs.rs#295)                        .to_string(),
[296](https://docs.rs#296)                )))
[297](https://docs.rs#297)            }
[298](https://docs.rs#298)        };
[299](https://docs.rs#299)        match emit::emit_kernel(f, compute_capability) {
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            Ok(primary) => Some(Ok(EmittedText {
[301](https://docs.rs#301)                primary,
[302](https://docs.rs#302)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA")],
[303](https://docs.rs#303)            })),
[304](https://docs.rs#304)            Err(e) => Some(Err(e)),
[305](https://docs.rs#305)        }
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    }
[307](https://docs.rs#307)}
[308](https://docs.rs#308)
[309](https://docs.rs#309)/// PMAT-961 — the anti-correlation witness's *general* emitter: xpile's OWN
[310](https://docs.rs#310)/// hand-emitted PTX for the fixed `out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1` saxpy kernel,
[311](https://docs.rs#311)/// independent of the module's contents (the witness drives a fixed kernel so
[312](https://docs.rs#312)/// the diff is reproducible). Computes `(x + x) + 1.0` over f64 — the exact
[313](https://docs.rs#313)/// numeric semantics of the nvcc CUDA-C peer, via a categorically different
[314](https://docs.rs#314)/// codegen path (xpile text vs nvcc C++).
[315](https://docs.rs#315)struct XpileSaxpyPtxEmitter;
[316](https://docs.rs#316)
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// The nvcc-compilable CUDA-C `xpile_kernel` for the canonical
[318](https://docs.rs#318)/// `out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1` saxpy kernel (the specialist half of the §29 PTX
[319](https://docs.rs#319)/// anti-correlation pair). `pub` so the PMAT-963 cross-hardware witness pairs
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// it with xpile's hand-emitted PTX and runs both on the gx10 (GB10 / sm_121)
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// fleet host — the same categorically-independent pair as the local sm_89
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// arm, on a different architecture.
[323](https://docs.rs#323)pub const SAXPY_CUDA_C_KERNEL: &str = "\
[324](https://docs.rs#324)__global__ void xpile_kernel(const float* in, float* out, int n) {
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    if (i < n) {
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        // general path: explicit multiply then add
[328](https://docs.rs#328)        out[i] = 2.0f * in[i] + 1.0f;
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    }
[330](https://docs.rs#330)}
[331](https://docs.rs#331)";
[332](https://docs.rs#332)
[333](https://docs.rs#333)/// Build the canonical `out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1` f64 kernel function the witness
[334](https://docs.rs#334)/// emitters share (so xpile PTX and nvcc CUDA-C attest the same semantics).
[335](https://docs.rs#335)/// `pub` so the PMAT-963 cross-hardware witness emits xpile's hand-emitted PTX
[336](https://docs.rs#336)/// for the gx10 (sm_121) target from the SAME meta-HIR the local sm_89 arm uses.
[337](https://docs.rs#337)pub fn saxpy_kernel_fn() -> Function {
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    let x_plus_x = Expr::FloatBinOp {
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        op: FloatOp::Add,
[340](https://docs.rs#340)        lhs: Box::new(Expr::Ident("x".into())),
[341](https://docs.rs#341)        rhs: Box::new(Expr::Ident("x".into())),
[342](https://docs.rs#342)    };
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    Function {
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        name: "xpile_kernel".into(),
[345](https://docs.rs#345)        params: vec![Param {
[346](https://docs.rs#346)            name: "x".into(),
[347](https://docs.rs#347)            ty: Type::F64,
[348](https://docs.rs#348)            mutable: false,
[349](https://docs.rs#349)        }],
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        return_type: Type::F64,
[351](https://docs.rs#351)        body: Block {
[352](https://docs.rs#352)            stmts: Vec::new(),
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            trailing_return: Expr::FloatBinOp {
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                op: FloatOp::Add,
[355](https://docs.rs#355)                lhs: Box::new(x_plus_x),
[356](https://docs.rs#356)                rhs: Box::new(Expr::LitFloat(1.0)),
[357](https://docs.rs#357)            },
[358](https://docs.rs#358)        },
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    }
[360](https://docs.rs#360)}
[361](https://docs.rs#361)
[362](https://docs.rs#362)impl TargetEmitter for XpileSaxpyPtxEmitter {

[373](https://docs.rs#373)            Some(HwProfile::Ptx { compute_capability }) => compute_capability,
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            _ => return Some(Err(BackendError::MissingHardware(Target::Ptx))),
[375](https://docs.rs#375)        };
[376](https://docs.rs#376)        match emit::emit_kernel(&saxpy_kernel_fn(), compute_capability) {
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            Ok(primary) => Some(Ok(EmittedText {
[378](https://docs.rs#378)                primary,
[379](https://docs.rs#379)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA")],
[380](https://docs.rs#380)            })),
[381](https://docs.rs#381)            Err(e) => Some(Err(e)),
[382](https://docs.rs#382)        }

[386](https://docs.rs#386)/// PMAT-962 — the control-flow anti-correlation witness's *general* emitter:
[387](https://docs.rs#387)/// xpile's OWN hand-emitted PTX for the relu kernel `out[i] = (in[i] > 0) ?
[388](https://docs.rs#388)/// in[i] : 0` — exercising the new `if`/`else` + `setp.gt.f64` + `@!%p bra`
[389](https://docs.rs#389)/// lowering, the categorical PTX twin of the nvcc CUDA-C `?:` peer.
[390](https://docs.rs#390)struct XpileReluPtxEmitter;
[391](https://docs.rs#391)
[392](https://docs.rs#392)/// Build the relu kernel `out[i] = (x > 0) ? x : 0` as meta-HIR — an `if`/`else`
[393](https://docs.rs#393)/// over a comparison into a shared local, the shape the PMAT-962 control-flow
[394](https://docs.rs#394)/// lowering compiles to `setp`/`@!%p bra`/labels.
[395](https://docs.rs#395)fn relu_kernel_fn() -> Function {
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    Function {
[397](https://docs.rs#397)        name: "xpile_kernel".into(),
[398](https://docs.rs#398)        params: vec![Param {
[399](https://docs.rs#399)            name: "x".into(),
[400](https://docs.rs#400)            ty: Type::F64,
[401](https://docs.rs#401)            mutable: false,
[402](https://docs.rs#402)        }],
[403](https://docs.rs#403)        return_type: Type::F64,
[404](https://docs.rs#404)        body: Block {
[405](https://docs.rs#405)            stmts: vec![
[406](https://docs.rs#406)                Stmt::Let {
[407](https://docs.rs#407)                    name: "r".into(),
[408](https://docs.rs#408)                    ty: Type::F64,
[409](https://docs.rs#409)                    value: Expr::LitFloat(0.0),
[410](https://docs.rs#410)                    mutable: true,
[411](https://docs.rs#411)                },
[412](https://docs.rs#412)                Stmt::If {
[413](https://docs.rs#413)                    cond: Expr::BinOp {
[414](https://docs.rs#414)                        op: BinOp::Gt,
[415](https://docs.rs#415)                        lhs: Box::new(Expr::Ident("x".into())),
[416](https://docs.rs#416)                        rhs: Box::new(Expr::LitFloat(0.0)),
[417](https://docs.rs#417)                    },
[418](https://docs.rs#418)                    then_body: vec![Stmt::Assign {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)                        name: "r".into(),
[420](https://docs.rs#420)                        value: Expr::Ident("x".into()),
[421](https://docs.rs#421)                    }],
[422](https://docs.rs#422)                    else_body: vec![Stmt::Assign {
[423](https://docs.rs#423)                        name: "r".into(),
[424](https://docs.rs#424)                        value: Expr::LitFloat(0.0),
[425](https://docs.rs#425)                    }],
[426](https://docs.rs#426)                },
[427](https://docs.rs#427)            ],
[428](https://docs.rs#428)            trailing_return: Expr::Ident("r".into()),
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        },
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    }
[431](https://docs.rs#431)}

[446](https://docs.rs#446)        };
[447](https://docs.rs#447)        match emit::emit_kernel(&relu_kernel_fn(), compute_capability) {
[448](https://docs.rs#448)            Ok(primary) => Some(Ok(EmittedText {
[449](https://docs.rs#449)                primary,
[450](https://docs.rs#450)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA")],

[457](https://docs.rs#457)/// PMAT-962 — the control-flow witness's *specialist* emitter: a complete
[458](https://docs.rs#458)/// nvcc-compilable CUDA-C `xpile_kernel` computing the SAME relu semantics
[459](https://docs.rs#459)/// (`out[i] = in[i] > 0 ? in[i] : 0`) via a C `?:` ternary — a categorically
[460](https://docs.rs#460)/// independent codegen path from xpile's hand-emitted branch PTX.
[461](https://docs.rs#461)struct CudaReluGeneralEmitter;
[462](https://docs.rs#462)
[463](https://docs.rs#463)impl TargetEmitter for CudaReluGeneralEmitter {
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    fn name(&self) -> &str {
[465](https://docs.rs#465)        "cuda-relu-general"
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    }
[467](https://docs.rs#467)
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    fn try_emit(
[469](https://docs.rs#469)        &self,
[470](https://docs.rs#470)        _module: &Module,
[471](https://docs.rs#471)        config: &BackendConfig,
[472](https://docs.rs#472)    ) -> Option<Result<EmittedText, BackendError>> {
[473](https://docs.rs#473)        match &config.hardware {
[474](https://docs.rs#474)            Some(HwProfile::Ptx { .. }) => {}
[475](https://docs.rs#475)            _ => return Some(Err(BackendError::MissingHardware(Target::Ptx))),
[476](https://docs.rs#476)        }
[477](https://docs.rs#477)        Some(Ok(EmittedText {
[478](https://docs.rs#478)            primary: "\
[479](https://docs.rs#479)__global__ void xpile_kernel(const float* in, float* out, int n) {
[480](https://docs.rs#480)    int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    if (i < n) {
[482](https://docs.rs#482)        // specialist path: a C ternary (independent of xpile's branch PTX)
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        float x = in[i];
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        out[i] = x > 0.0f ? x : 0.0f;
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    }
[486](https://docs.rs#486)}
[487](https://docs.rs#487)"
[488](https://docs.rs#488)            .to_string(),
[489](https://docs.rs#489)            citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA")],
[490](https://docs.rs#490)        }))
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    }
[492](https://docs.rs#492)}
[493](https://docs.rs#493)
[494](https://docs.rs#494)/// PMAT-280 — Mock GEMM specialist emitter.
[495](https://docs.rs#495)///
[496](https://docs.rs#496)/// Matches modules whose name starts with `matmul_` — the shape
[497](https://docs.rs#497)/// filter real specialists like `aprender-gpu` would use to claim
[498](https://docs.rs#498)/// the GEMM/MMA kernel domain. Returns `None` from `try_emit` for
[499](https://docs.rs#499)/// non-matching modules, letting the general emitter handle them.
[500](https://docs.rs#500)/// For matching modules, emits a distinct PTX text (different from
[501](https://docs.rs#501)/// the scaffold) so the `QuorumStatus::Multi` path is exercised
[502](https://docs.rs#502)/// under non-trivial divergence.
[503](https://docs.rs#503)///
[504](https://docs.rs#504)/// This is intentionally not a real GEMM emitter — its job is to
[505](https://docs.rs#505)/// prove that the `MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist` routing
[506](https://docs.rs#506)/// layer composes correctly with the existing `PtxBackend`. The
[507](https://docs.rs#507)/// future `aprender-gpu` integration plugs in via the same trait
[508](https://docs.rs#508)/// without touching `PtxBackend`'s public API.
[509](https://docs.rs#509)struct MatmulSpecialistEmitter;
[510](https://docs.rs#510)
[511](https://docs.rs#511)impl TargetEmitter for MatmulSpecialistEmitter {
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    fn name(&self) -> &str {
[513](https://docs.rs#513)        "matmul-specialist-mock"
[514](https://docs.rs#514)    }
[515](https://docs.rs#515)
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    fn try_emit(
[517](https://docs.rs#517)        &self,
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        module: &Module,
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        config: &BackendConfig,
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    ) -> Option<Result<EmittedText, BackendError>> {
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        if !module.name.starts_with("matmul_") {
[522](https://docs.rs#522)            return None;
[523](https://docs.rs#523)        }
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        let compute_capability = match &config.hardware {
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            Some(HwProfile::Ptx { compute_capability }) => compute_capability,
[526](https://docs.rs#526)            _ => return Some(Err(BackendError::MissingHardware(Target::Ptx))),
[527](https://docs.rs#527)        };
[528](https://docs.rs#528)        Some(Ok(EmittedText {
[529](https://docs.rs#529)            primary: format!(
[530](https://docs.rs#530)                "// matmul-specialist scaffold\n// module: {}\n// compute_capability: {}\n// TODO: emit mma.sync.aligned via aprender-gpu shape templates.\n",
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                module.name, compute_capability,
[532](https://docs.rs#532)            ),
[533](https://docs.rs#533)            citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA")],
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        }))
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    }
[536](https://docs.rs#536)}
[537](https://docs.rs#537)
[538](https://docs.rs#538)// ─── PMAT-949: real CUDA-C kernel emitters for the executed GPU witness ──
[539](https://docs.rs#539)//
[540](https://docs.rs#540)// Two emitters that produce COMPLETE, nvcc-compilable CUDA-C
[541](https://docs.rs#541)// `__global__ void xpile_kernel(const float* in, float* out, int n)`
[542](https://docs.rs#542)// kernels computing identical semantics — `out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1` — via
[543](https://docs.rs#543)// categorically different implementations. The general emitter uses an
[544](https://docs.rs#544)// explicit `mul`+`add`; the specialist uses the fused-multiply-add
[545](https://docs.rs#545)// intrinsic `fmaf`. Both are run on the GPU under the `DiffExec` quorum
[546](https://docs.rs#546)// (see [`PtxBackend::new_cuda_diffexec_witness`]); the engine asserts
[547](https://docs.rs#547)// their executed outputs agree within tolerance. The kernel name and
[548](https://docs.rs#548)// signature are the harness contract used by [`NvccCudaDiffExecEngine`].
[549](https://docs.rs#549)
[550](https://docs.rs#550)/// General CUDA-C emitter — `out[i] = 2.0f * in[i] + 1.0f` via an
[551](https://docs.rs#551)/// explicit multiply-then-add. Emits a complete nvcc-compilable kernel.
[552](https://docs.rs#552)struct CudaSaxpyGeneralEmitter;
[553](https://docs.rs#553)
[554](https://docs.rs#554)impl TargetEmitter for CudaSaxpyGeneralEmitter {
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    fn name(&self) -> &str {
[556](https://docs.rs#556)        "cuda-saxpy-general"
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    }
[558](https://docs.rs#558)
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    fn try_emit(
[560](https://docs.rs#560)        &self,
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        _module: &Module,
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        config: &BackendConfig,
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    ) -> Option<Result<EmittedText, BackendError>> {
[564](https://docs.rs#564)        match &config.hardware {
[565](https://docs.rs#565)            Some(HwProfile::Ptx { .. }) => {}
[566](https://docs.rs#566)            _ => return Some(Err(BackendError::MissingHardware(Target::Ptx))),
[567](https://docs.rs#567)        }
[568](https://docs.rs#568)        Some(Ok(EmittedText {
[569](https://docs.rs#569)            primary: SAXPY_CUDA_C_KERNEL.to_string(),
[570](https://docs.rs#570)            citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA")],
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        }))
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    }
[573](https://docs.rs#573)}
[574](https://docs.rs#574)
[575](https://docs.rs#575)/// Specialist CUDA-C emitter — same semantics (`out[i] = 2*in[i] + 1`)
[576](https://docs.rs#576)/// computed via the fused-multiply-add intrinsic `fmaf`. A
[577](https://docs.rs#577)/// categorically independent implementation: the `DiffExec` quorum runs
[578](https://docs.rs#578)/// both on the GPU and falsifies the contract if they diverge.
[579](https://docs.rs#579)struct CudaSaxpySpecialistEmitter;
[580](https://docs.rs#580)
[581](https://docs.rs#581)impl TargetEmitter for CudaSaxpySpecialistEmitter {
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    fn name(&self) -> &str {
[583](https://docs.rs#583)        "cuda-saxpy-specialist-fma"
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    }
[585](https://docs.rs#585)
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    fn try_emit(
[587](https://docs.rs#587)        &self,
[588](https://docs.rs#588)        _module: &Module,
[589](https://docs.rs#589)        config: &BackendConfig,
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    ) -> Option<Result<EmittedText, BackendError>> {
[591](https://docs.rs#591)        match &config.hardware {
[592](https://docs.rs#592)            Some(HwProfile::Ptx { .. }) => {}
[593](https://docs.rs#593)            _ => return Some(Err(BackendError::MissingHardware(Target::Ptx))),
[594](https://docs.rs#594)        }
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        Some(Ok(EmittedText {
[596](https://docs.rs#596)            primary: "\
[597](https://docs.rs#597)__global__ void xpile_kernel(const float* in, float* out, int n) {
[598](https://docs.rs#598)    int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    if (i < n) {
[600](https://docs.rs#600)        // specialist path: fused multiply-add intrinsic
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        out[i] = fmaf(2.0f, in[i], 1.0f);
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    }
[603](https://docs.rs#603)}
[604](https://docs.rs#604)"
[605](https://docs.rs#605)            .to_string(),
[606](https://docs.rs#606)            citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA")],
[607](https://docs.rs#607)        }))
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    }
[609](https://docs.rs#609)}
[610](https://docs.rs#610)
[611](https://docs.rs#611)// ─── PMAT-481: offline PTX well-formedness gate (§30 Track 4) ────────
[612](https://docs.rs#612)//
[613](https://docs.rs#613)// A *structural* check on emitted PTX text — it does NOT execute
[614](https://docs.rs#614)// anything and is not the model→emission gate (that is the `DiffExec`
[615](https://docs.rs#615)// slice, PMAT-488). It exists so that the moment a real emitter lands
[616](https://docs.rs#616)// (PMAT-485, the `nvptx64` path) its output is gated for well-formedness
[617](https://docs.rs#617)// on FREE CI, and the `ptxas`-assembles step (wired with that emitter)
[618](https://docs.rs#618)// derives its `-arch` from the same `compute_capability` checked here —
[619](https://docs.rs#619)// never a hard-coded `sm_80`. Callers gate on [`ptx_looks_real`] so the
[620](https://docs.rs#620)// v0.1.0 scaffold comment placeholder is never treated as real emission.
[621](https://docs.rs#621)
[622](https://docs.rs#622)/// Reasons emitted PTX text fails the [`validate_ptx`] well-formedness gate.
[623](https://docs.rs#623)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
[624](https://docs.rs#624)pub enum PtxValidationError {
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// No `.version` directive — not PTX at all (e.g. the scaffold placeholder).
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    MissingVersion,
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    /// No `.target` directive.
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    MissingTarget,
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// `.target` arch does not match the requested compute capability.
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    TargetMismatch { expected: String, found: String },
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    /// No `.address_size 64` directive.
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    MissingAddressSize,
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    /// No `.visible .entry` kernel entry point.
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    MissingEntry,
[635](https://docs.rs#635)}
[636](https://docs.rs#636)
[637](https://docs.rs#637)impl std::fmt::Display for PtxValidationError {
[638](https://docs.rs#638)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        match self {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            Self::MissingVersion => write!(f, "PTX is missing a `.version` directive"),
[641](https://docs.rs#641)            Self::MissingTarget => write!(f, "PTX is missing a `.target` directive"),
[642](https://docs.rs#642)            Self::TargetMismatch { expected, found } => write!(
[643](https://docs.rs#643)                f,
[644](https://docs.rs#644)                "PTX `.target {found}` does not match requested compute capability `{expected}`"
[645](https://docs.rs#645)            ),
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            Self::MissingAddressSize => write!(f, "PTX is missing `.address_size 64`"),
[647](https://docs.rs#647)            Self::MissingEntry => write!(f, "PTX has no `.visible .entry` kernel"),
[648](https://docs.rs#648)        }
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    }
[650](https://docs.rs#650)}
[651](https://docs.rs#651)
[652](https://docs.rs#652)impl std::error::Error for PtxValidationError {}
[653](https://docs.rs#653)
[654](https://docs.rs#654)/// `true` when `text` looks like real PTX (carries a `.version`
[655](https://docs.rs#655)/// directive) rather than the v0.1.0 scaffold comment placeholder.
[656](https://docs.rs#656)pub fn ptx_looks_real(text: &str) -> bool {
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    directive_present(text, ".version")
[658](https://docs.rs#658)}
[659](https://docs.rs#659)
[660](https://docs.rs#660)/// The `ptxas -arch=<…>` value for a PTX `.target` compute capability —
[661](https://docs.rs#661)/// **derived, never hard-coded** (PMAT-481). The `ptxas` assemble step uses
[662](https://docs.rs#662)/// this so the assembled arch always matches the emitted `.target`.
[663](https://docs.rs#663)pub fn ptxas_arch(compute_capability: &str) -> String {
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    format!("-arch={compute_capability}")
[665](https://docs.rs#665)}
[666](https://docs.rs#666)
[667](https://docs.rs#667)/// `true` when `ptxas` (the offline PTX assembler) is invocable — the gate for
[668](https://docs.rs#668)/// the PMAT-961 offline assemble-validation test. Mirrors the
[669](https://docs.rs#669)/// cc/wat2wasm/nvcc graceful-skip helpers: absence is a clean skip (free CI
[670](https://docs.rs#670)/// has no CUDA toolkit), presence assembles the emitted PTX for real. This is
[671](https://docs.rs#671)/// the PTX analog of `wat2wasm`-assembles-WAT / naga-validates-WGSL.
[672](https://docs.rs#672)pub fn ptxas_available() -> bool {
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    std::process::Command::new("ptxas")
[674](https://docs.rs#674)        .arg("--version")
[675](https://docs.rs#675)        .output()
[676](https://docs.rs#676)        .map(|o| o.status.success())
[677](https://docs.rs#677)        .unwrap_or(false)
[678](https://docs.rs#678)}
[679](https://docs.rs#679)
[680](https://docs.rs#680)/// PMAT-961 — assemble `ptx_text` with the real `ptxas` for `compute_capability`,
[681](https://docs.rs#681)/// returning `Ok(())` on a clean assemble or `Err(stderr)` on rejection. The
[682](https://docs.rs#682)/// caller gates on [`ptxas_available`] (graceful-skip). This is the offline
[683](https://docs.rs#683)/// validation step the WAT lane gets from `wat2wasm` and the WGSL lane from
[684](https://docs.rs#684)/// naga — proof the hand-emitted PTX is well-formed for the NVIDIA assembler,
[685](https://docs.rs#685)/// not just our own structural [`validate_ptx`] check.
[686](https://docs.rs#686)pub fn ptxas_assemble(ptx_text: &str, compute_capability: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
[688](https://docs.rs#688)    static SEQ: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    // Unique per call so parallel test threads in one process never collide on
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    // the scratch `.ptx`/`.cubin` paths.
[691](https://docs.rs#691)    let uniq = format!(
[692](https://docs.rs#692)        "{}-{}",
[693](https://docs.rs#693)        std::process::id(),
[694](https://docs.rs#694)        SEQ.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    );
[696](https://docs.rs#696)    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("xpile-ptxas-{uniq}"));
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| format!("create temp dir: {e}"))?;
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    let ptx_path = dir.join("xpile_kernel.ptx");
[699](https://docs.rs#699)    let out_path = dir.join("xpile_kernel.cubin");
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    std::fs::write(&ptx_path, ptx_text).map_err(|e| format!("write ptx: {e}"))?;
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    let out = std::process::Command::new("ptxas")
[702](https://docs.rs#702)        .arg(ptxas_arch(compute_capability))
[703](https://docs.rs#703)        .arg(&ptx_path)
[704](https://docs.rs#704)        .arg("-o")
[705](https://docs.rs#705)        .arg(&out_path)
[706](https://docs.rs#706)        .output()
[707](https://docs.rs#707)        .map_err(|e| format!("spawn ptxas: {e}"))?;
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    if out.status.success() {
[709](https://docs.rs#709)        Ok(())
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    } else {
[711](https://docs.rs#711)        Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).into_owned())
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    }
[713](https://docs.rs#713)}
[714](https://docs.rs#714)
[715](https://docs.rs#715)/// PMAT-481 — structural well-formedness check on emitted PTX text:
[716](https://docs.rs#716)/// `.version`, `.target` matching `compute_capability`, `.address_size
[717](https://docs.rs#717)/// 64`, and at least one `.visible .entry`. Pure text — no GPU, no
[718](https://docs.rs#718)/// `ptxas`. Gate on [`ptx_looks_real`] first so the scaffold placeholder
[719](https://docs.rs#719)/// is not treated as real emission.
[720](https://docs.rs#720)pub fn validate_ptx(text: &str, compute_capability: &str) -> Result<(), PtxValidationError> {
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    if !directive_present(text, ".version") {
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        return Err(PtxValidationError::MissingVersion);
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    }
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    let target = ptx_target_arch(text).ok_or(PtxValidationError::MissingTarget)?;
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    if target != compute_capability {
[726](https://docs.rs#726)        return Err(PtxValidationError::TargetMismatch {
[727](https://docs.rs#727)            expected: compute_capability.to_string(),
[728](https://docs.rs#728)            found: target,
[729](https://docs.rs#729)        });
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    }
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    if !directive_present(text, ".address_size 64") {
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        return Err(PtxValidationError::MissingAddressSize);
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    }
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    if !text.contains(".visible .entry") {
[735](https://docs.rs#735)        return Err(PtxValidationError::MissingEntry);
[736](https://docs.rs#736)    }
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    Ok(())
[738](https://docs.rs#738)}
[739](https://docs.rs#739)
[740](https://docs.rs#740)/// True when a non-comment line starts with `directive`.
[741](https://docs.rs#741)fn directive_present(text: &str, directive: &str) -> bool {
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    text.lines()
[743](https://docs.rs#743)        .map(str::trim)
[744](https://docs.rs#744)        .filter(|l| !l.starts_with("//"))
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        .any(|l| l.starts_with(directive))
[746](https://docs.rs#746)}
[747](https://docs.rs#747)
[748](https://docs.rs#748)/// Extract the arch token (e.g. `sm_80`) from the `.target` directive.
[749](https://docs.rs#749)fn ptx_target_arch(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
[750](https://docs.rs#750)    text.lines().map(str::trim).find_map(|l| {
[751](https://docs.rs#751)        if l.starts_with("//") {
[752](https://docs.rs#752)            return None;
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        }
[754](https://docs.rs#754)        let rest = l.strip_prefix(".target")?;
[755](https://docs.rs#755)        if !rest.is_empty() && !rest.starts_with(char::is_whitespace) {
[756](https://docs.rs#756)            return None; // e.g. `.target_foo` — not the directive
[757](https://docs.rs#757)        }
[758](https://docs.rs#758)        let arch = rest.trim().split([',', ' ']).next().unwrap_or("").trim();
[759](https://docs.rs#759)        (!arch.is_empty()).then(|| arch.to_string())
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    })
[761](https://docs.rs#761)}
[762](https://docs.rs#762)
[763](https://docs.rs#763)#[cfg(test)]
[764](https://docs.rs#764)mod tests {
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    use super::*;
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    use xpile_backend::{Profile, QuorumStatus};
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    use xpile_meta_hir::{Block, Expr, FloatOp, Function, Item, Param, SourceLang, Type};
[768](https://docs.rs#768)
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    /// A real element-wise kernel module: `def k(x: f64) -> f64: return
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    /// (x + x) + 1.0` — the scalar saxpy shape the real PTX emitter lowers.
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    fn dummy_module() -> Module {
[772](https://docs.rs#772)        Module {
[773](https://docs.rs#773)            name: "test_kernel".into(),
[774](https://docs.rs#774)            source_lang: SourceLang::Rust,
[775](https://docs.rs#775)            items: vec![Item::Function(kernel_fn("k"))],
[776](https://docs.rs#776)            ffi_boundaries: Vec::new(),
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        }
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    }
[779](https://docs.rs#779)
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    fn kernel_fn(name: &str) -> Function {
[781](https://docs.rs#781)        let x_plus_x = Expr::FloatBinOp {
[782](https://docs.rs#782)            op: FloatOp::Add,
[783](https://docs.rs#783)            lhs: Box::new(Expr::Ident("x".into())),
[784](https://docs.rs#784)            rhs: Box::new(Expr::Ident("x".into())),
[785](https://docs.rs#785)        };
[786](https://docs.rs#786)        Function {
[787](https://docs.rs#787)            name: name.into(),
[788](https://docs.rs#788)            params: vec![Param {
[789](https://docs.rs#789)                name: "x".into(),
[790](https://docs.rs#790)                ty: Type::F64,
[791](https://docs.rs#791)                mutable: false,
[792](https://docs.rs#792)            }],
[793](https://docs.rs#793)            return_type: Type::F64,
[794](https://docs.rs#794)            body: Block {
[795](https://docs.rs#795)                stmts: Vec::new(),
[796](https://docs.rs#796)                trailing_return: Expr::FloatBinOp {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)                    op: FloatOp::Add,
[798](https://docs.rs#798)                    lhs: Box::new(x_plus_x),
[799](https://docs.rs#799)                    rhs: Box::new(Expr::LitFloat(1.0)),
[800](https://docs.rs#800)                },
[801](https://docs.rs#801)            },
[802](https://docs.rs#802)        }
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    }
[804](https://docs.rs#804)

[811](https://docs.rs#811)            }),
[812](https://docs.rs#812)        }

[815](https://docs.rs#815)    #[test]
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    fn ptx_backend_emits_real_ptx_through_multi_emitter() {
[817](https://docs.rs#817)        let backend = PtxBackend::new();
[818](https://docs.rs#818)        let artifact = backend
[819](https://docs.rs#819)            .lower(&dummy_module(), &ptx_config("sm_80"))
[820](https://docs.rs#820)            .unwrap();
[821](https://docs.rs#821)        // Quorum status comes from the wrapped MultiEmitterBackend; the real
[822](https://docs.rs#822)        // emitter name is propagated.

[824](https://docs.rs#824)            artifact.quorum_status,

[827](https://docs.rs#827)            }
[828](https://docs.rs#828)        );
[829](https://docs.rs#829)        // Real PTX, not a placeholder: directives + load/compute/store.
[830](https://docs.rs#830)        assert!(artifact.primary.contains(".target sm_80"));
[831](https://docs.rs#831)        assert!(artifact.primary.contains(".visible .entry xpile_kernel"));
[832](https://docs.rs#832)        assert!(artifact.primary.contains("ld.global.f64"));
[833](https://docs.rs#833)        assert!(artifact.primary.contains("st.global.f64"));
[834](https://docs.rs#834)        assert!(ptx_looks_real(&artifact.primary));
[835](https://docs.rs#835)        assert_eq!(validate_ptx(&artifact.primary, "sm_80"), Ok(()));
[836](https://docs.rs#836)        assert!(artifact
[837](https://docs.rs#837)            .citations
[838](https://docs.rs#838)            .iter()
[839](https://docs.rs#839)            .any(|c| c.as_str() == "C-COMPILE-RUST-TO-PTX-MMA"));
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    }

[871](https://docs.rs#871)
[872](https://docs.rs#872)    /// PMAT-280 — Matmul-named modules route through the specialist
[873](https://docs.rs#873)    /// when the multi-emitter constructor is used. Under
[874](https://docs.rs#874)    /// `PreferSpecialist`, the artifact reports the specialist's name
[875](https://docs.rs#875)    /// and its emission body, not the scaffold's.
[876](https://docs.rs#876)    #[test]
[877](https://docs.rs#877)    fn matmul_module_routes_through_specialist_under_multi_emitter() {
[878](https://docs.rs#878)        let backend = PtxBackend::new_with_matmul_specialist();
[879](https://docs.rs#879)        let artifact = backend
[880](https://docs.rs#880)            .lower(&matmul_module(), &ptx_config("sm_80"))
[881](https://docs.rs#881)            .unwrap();
[882](https://docs.rs#882)        assert_eq!(
[883](https://docs.rs#883)            artifact.quorum_status,
[884](https://docs.rs#884)            QuorumStatus::Single {
[885](https://docs.rs#885)                emitter: "matmul-specialist-mock".to_string()
[886](https://docs.rs#886)            },
[887](https://docs.rs#887)            "PreferSpecialist with matching specialist should report Single {{ specialist }}"
[888](https://docs.rs#888)        );
[889](https://docs.rs#889)        assert!(
[890](https://docs.rs#890)            artifact.primary.contains("matmul-specialist"),
[891](https://docs.rs#891)            "primary should carry the specialist's emission body, got:\n{}",
[892](https://docs.rs#892)            artifact.primary,
[893](https://docs.rs#893)        );
[894](https://docs.rs#894)    }
[895](https://docs.rs#895)
[896](https://docs.rs#896)    /// PMAT-280 — Non-matmul modules fall back to the general (real PTX)
[897](https://docs.rs#897)    /// emitter even when the multi-emitter constructor is used. The
[898](https://docs.rs#898)    /// specialist returns `None` for unmatched shapes; the

[900](https://docs.rs#900)    #[test]

[903](https://docs.rs#903)        let artifact = backend
[904](https://docs.rs#904)            .lower(&dummy_module(), &ptx_config("sm_80"))
[905](https://docs.rs#905)            .unwrap();

[907](https://docs.rs#907)            artifact.quorum_status,
[908](https://docs.rs#908)            QuorumStatus::Single {

[911](https://docs.rs#911)            "non-matching specialist should let general emit; QuorumStatus should reflect general"
[912](https://docs.rs#912)        );

[914](https://docs.rs#914)            artifact.primary.contains(".visible .entry xpile_kernel"),

[916](https://docs.rs#916)            artifact.primary,
[917](https://docs.rs#917)        );
[918](https://docs.rs#918)    }
[919](https://docs.rs#919)
[920](https://docs.rs#920)    /// PMAT-280 — The multi-emitter constructor still advertises the
[921](https://docs.rs#921)    /// same target / name as the single-emitter constructor — the
[922](https://docs.rs#922)    /// specialist is internal routing, not a separate Backend.
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    #[test]

[929](https://docs.rs#929)    }
[930](https://docs.rs#930)
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    /// PMAT-280 — Same hardware-rejection eagerness regardless of
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    /// constructor. The wrapper rejects `None`-hardware inputs before
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    /// any emitter fires.
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    #[test]
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    fn multi_emitter_constructor_rejects_missing_hardware() {

[937](https://docs.rs#937)        let cfg = BackendConfig {
[938](https://docs.rs#938)            target: Target::Ptx,
[939](https://docs.rs#939)            profile: Profile::RustOut,
[940](https://docs.rs#940)            hardware: None,
[941](https://docs.rs#941)        };
[942](https://docs.rs#942)        let err = backend.lower(&matmul_module(), &cfg).unwrap_err();
[943](https://docs.rs#943)        assert!(matches!(err, BackendError::MissingHardware(Target::Ptx)));
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    }
[945](https://docs.rs#945)
[946](https://docs.rs#946)    // ─── PMAT-481: offline PTX well-formedness gate ─────────────────
[947](https://docs.rs#947)
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    /// A minimal but real PTX kernel, the shape `nvptx64-nvidia-cuda`
[949](https://docs.rs#949)    /// rustc emits (verified on-box) — what PMAT-485 will produce.
[950](https://docs.rs#950)    const GOLDEN_PTX_SM80: &str = "\
[951](https://docs.rs#951)//
[952](https://docs.rs#952)// Generated by LLVM NVPTX Back-End
[953](https://docs.rs#953)//
[954](https://docs.rs#954).version 6.0
[955](https://docs.rs#955).target sm_80
[956](https://docs.rs#956).address_size 64
[957](https://docs.rs#957)
[958](https://docs.rs#958)\t.visible .entry add_one(
[959](https://docs.rs#959)\t\t.param .u64 add_one_param_0
[960](https://docs.rs#960)\t)
[961](https://docs.rs#961)\t{
[962](https://docs.rs#962)\t\tret;
[963](https://docs.rs#963)\t}
[964](https://docs.rs#964)";
[965](https://docs.rs#965)
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    #[test]
[967](https://docs.rs#967)    fn validate_ptx_accepts_well_formed_kernel() {
[968](https://docs.rs#968)        assert_eq!(validate_ptx(GOLDEN_PTX_SM80, "sm_80"), Ok(()));
[969](https://docs.rs#969)    }
[970](https://docs.rs#970)
[971](https://docs.rs#971)    #[test]
[972](https://docs.rs#972)    fn ptx_looks_real_classifies_golden_vs_comment_only() {
[973](https://docs.rs#973)        assert!(ptx_looks_real(GOLDEN_PTX_SM80));
[974](https://docs.rs#974)        // A comment-only blob (the kind the retired v0.1.0 scaffold emitted)
[975](https://docs.rs#975)        // must NOT be treated as real PTX (so PMAT-481 never false-passes).
[976](https://docs.rs#976)        let comment_only = "// just a comment\n// no .version directive\n";
[977](https://docs.rs#977)        assert!(!ptx_looks_real(comment_only));
[978](https://docs.rs#978)    }
[979](https://docs.rs#979)
[980](https://docs.rs#980)    #[test]
[981](https://docs.rs#981)    fn real_emitter_output_passes_validate_ptx() {
[982](https://docs.rs#982)        // The PMAT-961 real emitter produces PTX that passes the offline
[983](https://docs.rs#983)        // well-formedness gate (the retired scaffold's comment placeholder
[984](https://docs.rs#984)        // would have failed MissingVersion).
[985](https://docs.rs#985)        let ptx = PtxBackend::new()
[986](https://docs.rs#986)            .lower(&dummy_module(), &ptx_config("sm_89"))
[987](https://docs.rs#987)            .unwrap()
[988](https://docs.rs#988)            .primary;
[989](https://docs.rs#989)        assert!(ptx_looks_real(&ptx));
[990](https://docs.rs#990)        assert_eq!(validate_ptx(&ptx, "sm_89"), Ok(()));
[991](https://docs.rs#991)        // A comment-only blob still fails MissingVersion (negative coverage).
[992](https://docs.rs#992)        assert_eq!(
[993](https://docs.rs#993)            validate_ptx("// comment only\n", "sm_89"),
[994](https://docs.rs#994)            Err(PtxValidationError::MissingVersion)
[995](https://docs.rs#995)        );
[996](https://docs.rs#996)    }
[997](https://docs.rs#997)
[998](https://docs.rs#998)    #[test]
[999](https://docs.rs#999)    fn validate_ptx_detects_target_mismatch() {

[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)            validate_ptx(GOLDEN_PTX_SM80, "sm_90"),

# emit_kernel in xpile_ptx_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ptx-codegen/0.1.615/xpile_ptx_codegen/fn.emit_kernel.html

```
pub fn emit_kernel(
    f: &
```
[Function](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Function.html),
    compute_capability: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [BackendError](https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_backend/enum.BackendError.html)>## Expand description

Lower a meta-HIR [ Function](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Function.html) of the element-wise kernel shape to a
complete PTX module string targeting

`compute_capability` (e.g. `sm_89`).`compute_capability` is threaded verbatim into the `.target` directive —
**derived from **.

`xpile_backend::HwProfile::Ptx`, never hard-codedPMAT-980: a kernel whose parameters are `list[scalar]` arrays routes to the
array element-wise path ([`emit_array_kernel`]), where each list rides a
`.u64` global base pointer and `xs[i]` (at the per-thread index) lowers to
an `ld.global`. A kernel of bare scalar params keeps the original implicit
element-wise lowering below.
